blocks.en: 💧 Worship — Unit 9: The Ordinances
blocks.es_reference: 💧 Adoración — Unidad 9: Las Ordenanzas

blocks.en: Chapala Theological Seminary, a ministry of Common Ground Fellowship | Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Seminario Teológico de Chapala, un ministerio de Common Ground Fellowship | Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: This course is drawn from the worship curriculum of Dr. Wayne Cook, who served eleven years as Professor of Pastoral Ministries and Preaching, together with the teaching of Andi Cook, who taught alongside him at the seminary. It reflects not only academic study but decades of pastoral and seminary experience.
blocks.es_reference: Este curso proviene del currículo de adoración del Dr. Wayne Cook, quien sirvió once años como Profesor de Ministerios Pastorales y Predicación, junto con la enseñanza de Andi Cook, quien enseñó a su lado en el seminario. Refleja no solo el estudio académico sino décadas de experiencia pastoral y de seminario.

blocks.en: I. Baptism: A Public Confession
blocks.es_reference: I. El bautismo: una confesión pública

blocks.en: We turn now to the two ordinances, baptism and the Lord's Supper. Begin with baptism, which is a public confession of faith. It symbolizes being buried with Christ in His death and raised to walk in the newness of His likeness. The believer goes down into the water and is raised again, picturing death and resurrection. Mark this well: baptism does not save. It confesses a salvation already received. It is a symbol performed before the gathered church, by which the believer identifies himself publicly with the death and resurrection of Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Nos volvemos ahora a las dos ordenanzas, el bautismo y la Cena del Señor. Comience con el bautismo, que es una confesión pública de fe. Simboliza ser sepultado con Cristo en Su muerte y resucitado para andar en la novedad de Su semejanza. El creyente baja al agua y es levantado de nuevo, representando muerte y resurrección. Marque bien esto: el bautismo no salva. Confiesa una salvación ya recibida. Es un símbolo realizado ante la iglesia reunida, por el cual el creyente se identifica públicamente con la muerte y resurrección de Cristo.

blocks.en: The proper mode of baptism is immersion. The Greek word baptizo means to dip or to immerse, and immersion alone pictures the burial and the rising. Pouring or sprinkling cannot show what immersion shows. When the believer is lowered beneath the water and lifted up again, the whole congregation sees the gospel acted out: death to sin, and new life in Christ.
blocks.es_reference: El modo apropiado del bautismo es la inmersión. La palabra griega baptizo significa sumergir o zambullir, y solo la inmersión representa la sepultura y el resucitar. Derramar o rociar no puede mostrar lo que la inmersión muestra. Cuando el creyente es bajado bajo el agua y levantado de nuevo, toda la congregación ve el evangelio representado: muerte al pecado, y nueva vida en Cristo.

blocks.en: II. The Room and the Amen
blocks.es_reference: II. La sala y el Amén

blocks.en: Here is where the architecture begins to preach, a theme we will develop fully in Unit 10. In a believer's-baptism church the baptistry is prominent and central, usually behind the pulpit and often elevated, so that the whole congregation can see the baptism. That placement is not an accident of building design; it is theology in wood and water. Because baptism is a public confession before the gathered church, the room is built to make it visible.
blocks.es_reference: Aquí es donde la arquitectura comienza a predicar, un tema que desarrollaremos plenamente en la Unidad 10. En una iglesia que practica el bautismo del creyente, el baptisterio es prominente y central, usualmente detrás del púlpito y a menudo elevado, para que toda la congregación pueda ver el bautismo. Esa colocación no es un accidente del diseño del edificio; es teología en madera y agua. Porque el bautismo es una confesión pública ante la iglesia reunida, la sala se construye para hacerlo visible.

blocks.en: Watch what happens at the moment of baptism. The pastor speaks the words, buried with Christ in His death and raised to walk in His likeness, and then he turns to the congregation and says, "And all the people say," and the church answers, "Amen." That congregational Amen is the family of God confessing what has happened. The believer has identified with Christ, and the church has witnessed it and ratified it together. Baptism is never a private affair. The whole body says Amen.
blocks.es_reference: Observe lo que sucede en el momento del bautismo. El pastor pronuncia las palabras, sepultado con Cristo en Su muerte y resucitado para andar en Su semejanza, y luego se vuelve a la congregación y dice, "Y todo el pueblo diga," y la iglesia responde, "Amén." Ese Amén congregacional es la familia de Dios confesando lo que ha sucedido. El creyente se ha identificado con Cristo, y la iglesia lo ha presenciado y ratificado junta. El bautismo nunca es un asunto privado. Todo el cuerpo dice Amén.

blocks.en: Contrast this with the Catholic font, which is usually small and set off to one side near the entrance. The placement preaches a different theology. For the Catholic, baptism is the rite of entry into the church, typically administered to an infant, and it is believed to convey saving grace and wash away original sin. The believer's-baptism church's baptistry, central and visible, preaches that baptism is the public confession of a believer who already has faith — a conviction shared across many evangelical traditions, not one alone. Same ordinance, opposite theologies, and you can read the difference in where the water sits in the room.
blocks.es_reference: Contraste esto con la pila católica, que usualmente es pequeña y está colocada a un lado cerca de la entrada. La colocación predica una teología diferente. Para el católico, el bautismo es el rito de entrada a la iglesia, típicamente administrado a un infante, y se cree que confiere gracia salvadora y lava el pecado original. El baptisterio de una iglesia que practica el bautismo del creyente, central y visible, predica que el bautismo es la confesión pública de un creyente que ya tiene fe — una convicción compartida por muchas tradiciones evangélicas, no una sola. La misma ordenanza, teologías opuestas, y usted puede leer la diferencia en dónde se sitúa el agua en la sala.

blocks.en: III. The Lord's Supper: Memorial and Proclamation
blocks.es_reference: III. La Cena del Señor: memorial y proclamación

blocks.en: The Lord's Supper is a memorial and a proclamation. We observe it in remembrance of Christ, as He commanded. The bread represents His body and the cup His blood, given for us. Paul tells us that as often as we eat the bread and drink the cup, we proclaim the Lord's death until He comes. So the Supper looks in two directions at once: back to the cross, and forward to His return.
blocks.es_reference: La Cena del Señor es un memorial y una proclamación. La observamos en memoria de Cristo, como Él mandó. El pan representa Su cuerpo y la copa Su sangre, dados por nosotros. Pablo nos dice que todas las veces que comemos el pan y bebemos la copa, proclamamos la muerte del Señor hasta que venga. Así que la Cena mira en dos direcciones a la vez: atrás a la cruz, y adelante a Su regreso.

blocks.en: Once again the placement of the furniture preaches. Where you put the Lord's Supper table declares a theology before you say a word. In a Protestant sanctuary the communion table sits centered but below the pulpit, declaring that the Word is elevated above the sacrament. In a Catholic church the altar stands front and center, declaring that the saving sacrament is central. The table below the pulpit and the altar front and center are two different gospels in furniture.
blocks.es_reference: Una vez más la colocación del mobiliario predica. Donde coloque la mesa de la Cena del Señor declara una teología antes de que diga una palabra. En un santuario protestante la mesa de comunión se sitúa centrada pero debajo del púlpito, declarando que la Palabra está elevada sobre el sacramento. En una iglesia católica el altar está al frente y al centro, declarando que el sacramento salvador es central. La mesa debajo del púlpito y el altar al frente y al centro son dos evangelios diferentes en el mobiliario.

blocks.en: IV. Ordinances, Not Sacraments
blocks.es_reference: IV. Ordenanzas, no sacramentos

blocks.en: Believer's-baptism evangelicals deliberately call these two acts ordinances rather than sacraments, and the word matters. A sacrament, in Catholic theology, is a channel that conveys saving grace. An ordinance is something Christ ordained and commanded for us to obey. The ordinances symbolize and memorialize; they do not save. That is precisely why we use the word ordinance, to confess that baptism and the Lord's Supper are commanded symbols of obedience, not means of grace.
blocks.es_reference: Los evangélicos que practican el bautismo del creyente deliberadamente llaman a estos dos actos ordenanzas en lugar de sacramentos, y la palabra importa. Un sacramento, en la teología católica, es un canal que confiere gracia salvadora. Una ordenanza es algo que Cristo ordenó y mandó para que obedezcamos. Las ordenanzas simbolizan y conmemoran; no salvan. Esa es precisamente la razón por la que usamos la palabra ordenanza, para confesar que el bautismo y la Cena del Señor son símbolos mandados de obediencia, no medios de gracia.

blocks.en: Both ordinances must be administered reverently, with preparation and clear explanation, so that they remain meaningful acts of worship rather than empty ritual. When the pastor explains their meaning, the people grasp the gospel they picture. And that is the final point: both ordinances make the gospel visible. Baptism shows the believer's death, burial, and resurrection with Christ. The Lord's Supper shows Christ's body broken and blood shed for sin. Together they preach the gospel without words, so that in worship the people do not only hear the gospel, they see it.
blocks.es_reference: Ambas ordenanzas deben administrarse reverentemente, con preparación y explicación clara, para que permanezcan como actos significativos de adoración en lugar de ritual vacío. Cuando el pastor explica su significado, el pueblo capta el evangelio que representan. Y ese es el punto final: ambas ordenanzas hacen visible el evangelio. El bautismo muestra la muerte, sepultura, y resurrección del creyente con Cristo. La Cena del Señor muestra el cuerpo de Cristo partido y la sangre derramada por el pecado. Juntas predican el evangelio sin palabras, para que en la adoración el pueblo no solo oiga el evangelio, sino que lo vea.

sa.prompt: Explain the meaning of baptism as a public confession of faith, including its symbolism of death and resurrection.
sa.model: Baptism is a public confession of faith, symbolizing being buried with Christ in His death and raised to walk in the newness of His likeness. The believer goes down into the water and is raised again, picturing death and resurrection. Baptism does not save; it confesses a salvation already received, identifying the believer publicly with Christ's death and resurrection before the gathered church.

sa.prompt: Describe how the architecture of the baptistry in a believer's-baptism church reflects its theology of baptism.
sa.model: The baptistry is placed prominently and centrally, usually behind the pulpit and often elevated, so the whole congregation can see the baptism. This placement is not accidental but theology in wood and water: because baptism is a public confession before the gathered church, the room is deliberately built to make it visible to everyone rather than tucked away out of sight.

sa.prompt: Describe the baptism scene and the congregational 'Amen,' and explain what it confesses.
sa.model: At the moment of baptism, the pastor speaks the words 'buried with Christ in His death and raised to walk in His likeness,' then turns to the congregation and says, 'And all the people say,' and the church answers, 'Amen.' That congregational Amen confesses that the family of God has witnessed and ratified together what has happened — baptism is never a private affair, since the whole body affirms it.

sa.prompt: Contrast believer's-baptism practice with the Catholic font and infant baptism, and explain the different theology each reflects.
sa.model: The Catholic font is usually small and set off to one side near the entrance, reflecting a theology where baptism is the rite of entry into the church, typically administered to an infant, believed to convey saving grace and wash away original sin. The central, visible believer's-baptism baptistry instead preaches that baptism is the public confession of a believer who already has faith — the same ordinance, but opposite theologies, readable simply in where the water sits in the room.

sa.prompt: Explain the meaning of the Lord's Supper as a memorial and proclamation.
sa.model: The Lord's Supper is a memorial and a proclamation. We observe it in remembrance of Christ, as He commanded, with the bread representing His body and the cup His blood, given for us. Paul tells us that as often as we eat the bread and drink the cup, we proclaim the Lord's death until He comes, so the Supper looks in two directions at once: back to the cross and forward to His return.

sa.prompt: How does the placement of the Lord's Supper table in a sanctuary reflect a theology?
sa.model: In a Protestant sanctuary the communion table sits centered but below the pulpit, declaring that the Word is elevated above the sacrament. In a Catholic church the altar stands front and center, declaring that the saving sacrament is central. The table below the pulpit and the altar front and center preach two different gospels through nothing but furniture placement.

sa.prompt: Why are baptism and the Lord's Supper called ordinances rather than sacraments in the believer's-baptism tradition?
sa.model: These two acts are called ordinances rather than sacraments because a sacrament, in Catholic theology, is a channel that conveys saving grace, while an ordinance is something Christ ordained and commanded for us to obey. The ordinances symbolize and memorialize; they do not save — the word 'ordinance' confesses that baptism and the Lord's Supper are commanded symbols of obedience, not means of grace.

sa.prompt: What is the proper mode of baptism in the believer's-baptism tradition, and why?
sa.model: The proper mode of baptism is immersion, since the Greek word baptizo means to dip or to immerse, and immersion alone pictures the burial and the rising with Christ. Pouring or sprinkling cannot show what immersion shows; when the believer is lowered beneath the water and lifted up again, the whole congregation sees the gospel of death to sin and new life in Christ acted out visually.

sa.prompt: How should the ordinances be administered so they remain meaningful acts of worship?
sa.model: Both ordinances must be administered reverently, with preparation and clear explanation, so that they remain meaningful acts of worship rather than empty ritual. When the pastor explains their meaning ahead of time, the people grasp the gospel they picture, rather than watching a rite performed hastily or without context.

sa.prompt: Summarize how both ordinances make the gospel visible in worship.
sa.model: Both ordinances make the gospel visible in worship: baptism shows the believer's death, burial, and resurrection with Christ, while the Lord's Supper shows Christ's body broken and blood shed for sin. Together they preach the gospel without words, so that in worship the people do not only hear the gospel, they see it acted out before them.
